text:
chris-customer: Hi team — escalating: after onboarding our service behind PrivateLink (account A) and sharing the interface endpoint with customer account B, traffic from B intermittently fails with 502 / TLS handshake errors. Customer trace shows DNS sometimes resolving to public IP and sometimes to vpce, then failures. They see 'tls: handshake failure' in client logs.

maria-support: Thanks Chris — can you paste a short repro (curl + dig) and confirm whether private DNS was enabled when the endpoint was created? Also which endpoint type (interface vs gateway) and LB type?

chris-customer: Repro below (from an instance in acct-B):
```
$ dig svc.prod.internal +short
10.12.5.6
52.12.34.56   <-- unexpected public IP
\n$ curl -v https://svc.prod.internal/health
* TLS handshake error: tls: handshake failure\n* Failed to connect
```
We created an interface endpoint (vpce-0abc) in acct-A fronted by an NLB. Private DNS was not explicitly enabled during create (we used console share).

dinesh-eng: Quick notes: cross-account interface endpoints do NOT magically populate private hosted zones in the consumer account. There are two common patterns that break DNS:
- Consumer (acct-B) still resolves to the public A record because Private DNS association to the VPC wasn't set up.
- Split-horizon/PHZ conflict where Route53 hosted zone in acct-B shadows the private DNS.

Check: `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0abc` and look for "PrivateDnsEnabled": true/false and the list of "PrivateDnsNames".

Also run from acct-B: `aws route53resolver list-resolver-endpoint-ip-addresses --filters Name=ResolverEndpointId,Values=...` if using inbound endpoints.

sam-netops: Also verify sg and route table: interface endpoints require the consumer's ENIs to reach the endpoint on port 443 (or whatever TLS port). Common failure is egress policy sending traffic out via NAT (and hitting public IP) instead of EVP/VPCE because route table points to NAT GW for that subnet.

infra-bot: Note: NLB listeners in TLS passthrough mode do not terminate TLS — cert must be on the target if using TLS to targets. If you intended to terminate on the LB, use TLS listener with cert on the NLB or deploy an ALB. PrivateLink supports NLB as service network load balancer only (for non-HTTP case, ALB-backed endpoints have other constraints).

maria-support: Based on the info so far, checklist for customer: (1) enable Private DNS for the endpoint in provider account and share the endpoint so consumer can create association, OR ask consumer to create a Route53 PHZ and associate the VPC; (2) ensure no public/PHZ conflict for the same name; (3) check consumer VPC route table doesn't send traffic via NAT to internet; (4) ensure SGs allow TLS (443) between consumer subnets and endpoint ENIs; (5) confirm NLB vs ALB TLS termination expectation.

chris-customer: Tried enabling Private DNS in acct-A and asked acct-B to disassociate their public hosted zone. After that `dig` resolves to a VPCE private IP consistently and `curl -v` now shows normal TLS handshake: `SSL handshake ok`, 200. Customer confirms stable.

dinesh-eng: Great. For postmortem + KB: note that creating an interface endpoint and sharing it does not automatically update consumer account DNS unless Private DNS is enabled and associations are created. If you need cross-account resolution without changing consumer hosted zones, either enable Private DNS + shared association or publish a shared Route53 hosted zone and have consumer associate.

maria-support: Action items: Chris — please paste the vpce id and whether you changed the NLB listener mode so we can close this. Also add a short blurb to support KB about route table vs NAT pitfalls.

chris-customer: vpce-0abc1234, we flipped PrivateDnsEnabled=true and removed conflicting public PHZ in acct-B. No change to NLB listeners. Closing as resolved. :tada:

sam-netops: Added a note to internal KB: "Shared VPCE DNS origin gotcha — consumer PHZ can shadow private DNS; check route tables for NAT egress". :white_check_mark:
